text:
incident-bot: ALERT (sev=high) — tail latency spike observed for inference service in us‑east-1. Metric: 95th/99th latency on /v1/generate rose ~4x vs baseline starting 1778881200. Impact: increased error/retry rate for some customers; autoscaling not bringing latency down. Investigating.

alice.choi: ack. paging oncall. tagging eng-sre for network/infra triage. any immediate mitigations we can try to reduce customer impact?

ben.smyth: looking. quick summary: heap on compute looks fine, load balancing healthy. seeing network transmit queues growing on a subset of inf-prod-us-east hosts. kernel logs show TCP retransmit bursts and NIC drops. not seeing KV cache evictions or model OOMs.

ben.smyth: paste logs:
```
Mar 24 12:34:56 inf-prod-ue1-07 kernel: eth0: tx_queue_len exceeded, dropped packets=8432
Mar 24 12:35:03 inf-prod-ue1-09 kernel: tcp: excessive retransmits detected from 10.0.4.21
Mar 24 12:35:10 envoy[2156]: upstream connect failure: network error, connection reset
```

carla.ops: can we shift traffic off the impacted host group or reroute to us-east-2/us-west while we confirm root cause? Prefer avoiding full region failover; a weighted reroute would be ideal.

ben.smyth: yes — we can update the routing policy in control plane to reduce weight for the affected host pool. command to dim weight via control API (temporary patch):
```bash
curl -X POST "https://control.redwood.internal/api/v1/routes/adjust" \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $CTRL_TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"route":"us-east-1/generate","adjustments":[{"pool":"inf-prod-ue1","weight":0.2}]}'
```
I'll stage that change in 60s if no objections.

alice.choi: go ahead. please annotate the change with rollback tag `network-tail-burst`. notify infra once applied.

deploy-bot: CONFIG_CHANGE: routing adjustment queued by ben.smyth. Change id: rchg-20240324-01. Scheduled in 60s.

ben.smyth: applied. rchg-20240324-01 -> success. lowering weight for inf-prod-ue1 to 0.2.

carla.ops: confirmed traffic shift starting. seeing reduced connections on inf-prod-ue1 hosts. :thumbsup: please update status page copy so customer-facing comms align.

dan.pmo: DRAFT status page update (customer-facing):
"We are currently investigating intermittent increases in request latency for the inference API (us‑east). Some requests may experience higher delay or transient errors. Our engineers have implemented a temporary traffic reroute to reduce impact while we investigate a network-level issue in a subset of hosts. We expect continued mitigation activity over the next 30–45 minutes. No action required on customer side; we will post updates here as we know more."

alice.choi: nice. include estimated ETA and note that embeddings and non-realtime batch endpoints are unaffected. add contact link for support if customers are significantly impacted.

dan.pmo: updated: "ETA for primary mitigation: 30–45 minutes. Affected endpoints: low-volume subset of realtime generation traffic in us‑east. Non-realtime batch/embeddings unaffected. For urgent impact, contact support@redwood.ai"

jen.night: I can take handoff in 15m for overnight monitoring. please provide a one-line summary + link to runbook so I can pick up.

ben.smyth: one-liner: "Network transmit queue drops on a host pool in us‑east causing tail-latency spikes; temporary traffic weight reduction applied to pool inf-prod-ue1; monitoring for improvement and NIC driver/hypervisor anomalies." Runbook: https://runbooks.redwood.internal/infra/network-tail-burst (see steps: check `tx_drops`, adjust weights, rollback change id rchg-20240324-01).

alice.choi: handing off to jen.night in 15m. jen — I'll DM you the incident bridge and current traces. leave any final notes in this thread before you take over.

ben.smyth: current metrics: 95th latency down ~32% versus peak after reroute; 99th still ~1.8x baseline. continuing analysis on NIC/host OS side and engaging cloud provider on potential noisy neighbor on host hw.

carla.ops: start capturing pcap from affected host group and upload to secure bucket for provider review.

ben.smyth: started pcaps → s3://redwood-internal/pcaps/1778881234/ (access: infra-team only).

deploy-bot: NOTE: no model code was deployed during this window. only routing policy changes.

alice.choi: thanks everyone — we have a partial mitigation in place and a handoff plan. leave this thread open for any follow-ups; jen will post final resolution/retrospective once provider confirm root cause.

jen.night: taking over. will monitor for 60m then escalate if 99th doesn't drop below 1.2x baseline. tagging ops for follow-up tomorrow morning.
